questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Post-Mauryan Period and Regional Powers' refers to.
questions.a: After the fall of the Mauryan Empire around 185 BCE, India entered a period of political fragmentation and reorganisation. Multiple regional powers emerged, including the Shungas in the north, the Satavahanas in the Deccan, the Indo-Greeks and Kushanas in the northwest, and various dynasties in the south.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Post-Mauryan Period and Regional Powers'.
questions.a: The post-Mauryan period was characterised by the rise of multiple regional kingdoms, foreign invasions in the north, and flourishing trade and cultural exchange across regions.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Post-Mauryan Period and Regional Powers' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Political Reorganisation after the Mauryas

concepts.title: Sangam Age and the Tamil Kingdoms

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sangam Age and the Tamil Kingdoms' refers to.
questions.a: The Sangam Age (approximately 300 BCE to 300 CE) was a period of literary and cultural flourishing in southern India, centred in Madurai. Three Tamil kingdoms ruled the region: the Cheras (Kerala region), the Cholas (northern Tamil Nadu), and the Pandyas (southern Tamil Nadu). The Sangam assemblies patronised Tamil literature.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sangam Age and the Tamil Kingdoms'.
questions.a: The three Tamil kingdoms of Cheras, Cholas, and Pandyas flourished during the Sangam Age, which produced a rich body of Tamil literature and a distinctive cultural tradition.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Sangam Age and the Tamil Kingdoms' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Sangam Age: Cheras, Cholas, and Pandyas

concepts.title: The Silk Route and Trade Connections

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Silk Route and Trade Connections' refers to.
questions.a: The Silk Route was a network of trade routes connecting China to the Mediterranean through Central Asia, India, and Persia. It facilitated the exchange of silk, spices, precious stones, and ideas. The Kushanas controlled key segments of this route, benefiting from tolls and trade revenues.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Silk Route and Trade Connections'.
questions.a: The Silk Route linked East and West, enabling not just trade in goods but also the exchange of religions, technologies, and cultural ideas, with the Kushanas playing a key intermediary role.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Silk Route and Trade Connections' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Trade Networks: The Silk Route

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Kanishka and the Kushana Empire' refers to.
questions.a: Kanishka was the most famous ruler of the Kushana Empire, ruling around the 1st or 2nd century CE. His empire extended from Central Asia to northern India. He was a great patron of Buddhism, convened the Fourth Buddhist Council, and promoted the Gandhara school of art.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Kanishka and the Kushana Empire'.
questions.a: Kanishka's reign marked the peak of the Kushana Empire, characterised by religious patronage, cultural synthesis, and the promotion of Buddhism and art.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Kanishka and the Kushana Empire' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Kushana Empire under Kanishka

concepts.title: Gandhara and Mathura Schools of Art

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Gandhara and Mathura Schools of Art' refers to.
questions.a: The Gandhara school of art flourished in the northwest (modern Pakistan and Afghanistan) under Kushana patronage, blending Greek and Indian styles to create the earliest Buddha images. The Mathura school, centred in Mathura, developed an indigenous style of sculpture depicting Buddha, Jain tirthankaras, and Hindu deities.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Gandhara and Mathura Schools of Art'.
questions.a: The Gandhara and Mathura schools represent two distinct artistic traditions of the Kushana period, one influenced by Greco-Roman styles and the other by indigenous Indian traditions.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Gandhara and Mathura Schools of Art' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Art and Sculpture: Gandhara and Mathura

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Southern Dynasties and their Contributions' refers to.
questions.a: Besides the Satavahanas, several dynasties ruled southern India during this period, including the Cheras, Cholas, and Pandyas of the Sangam Age. They contributed to trade with Rome and Southeast Asia, built ports like Muziris and Puhar, and patronised Tamil literature and temple culture.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Southern Dynasties and their Contributions'.
questions.a: The southern dynasties fostered maritime trade, Tamil literature, and early temple traditions, establishing the foundations of south Indian cultural and economic life.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Southern Dynasties and their Contributions' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Southern India: Regional Dynasties

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Cultural Developments in the Period' refers to.
questions.a: The post-Mauryan period saw significant cultural developments including the growth of Sanskrit literature, the compilation of the Ramayana and Mahabharata, advances in astronomy and medicine, the emergence of new art forms, and the rise of Bhakti traditions that emphasised personal devotion to deities.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Cultural Developments in the Period'.
questions.a: The Age of Reorganisation was culturally vibrant, with developments in literature, science, art, and religion that shaped the course of Indian civilisation for centuries.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Cultural Developments in the Period' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Cultural and Intellectual Developments
